title: Rapid Needs Assessment: Flood Response in Kasoro District

headings.text: Rapid Needs Assessment: Flood Response in Kasoro District

key_sentences: Heavy rains between 28 September and 3 October caused the Kasoro River to overflow its banks in four sub-counties.
An estimated 4,870 households were affected, of whom 1,215 are currently displaced in schools, churches and host families.
Displaced families occupy 31 classrooms, with an average of 14 households per room.
The Programme Quality Unit will review this report on 14 October and submit a funding request to the emergency pooled fund.
A follow-up assessment of Ongora is planned once the road to the two cut-off parishes reopens.

list_items.text: Shelter is the most urgent need: 62% of displaced households sleep in overcrowded classrooms.
Seven of eleven boreholes in the flooded area are contaminated or inaccessible.
Standing maize ready for harvest was lost on about 1,900 hectares.
Two health centres remain functional but have run out of oral rehydration salts.
Distribute emergency shelter kits and non-food items to all 1,215 displaced households within ten days.
Prioritise Ongora and Kidera, where crowding is worst.
Coordinate with the Red Cross to avoid double distribution.
Restore safe water at displacement sites.
Chlorinate and disinfect the seven affected boreholes.
Install emergency latrines and handwashing stations at the 14 sites.
Provide a one-month food ration or cash transfer to displaced households.
Supply both health centres with oral rehydration salts, zinc and malaria test kits.
